text.p: U.S. company Anixter International Inc aims to lead the Asia-Pacific region in computer network integration by the year 2001, a senior company official said on Thursday.
In the current financial year, revenue from the Asia-Pacific is expected to grow by more than 50 percent from US$100 million.

"Anixter has determined that we want to be the market leader in providing products and solutions and education services in network infrastructure," K.H. Wun, president of Anixter, Asia-Pacific, told Reuters in an interview.
"In the Asia-Pacific, we want to be the market leader in four years' time by year 2001."
He said leadership would be measured in terms of revenue and level of customer satisfaction.
"Last year, Asia-Pacific saw 35-40 percent growth. This year the growth rate will be in excess of 50 percent," Wun said.

Anixter recorded revenue of US$2.5 billion for the financial year ended January 3, 1997, with a contribution from the Asia-Pacific of about US$100 million. The bulk of revenue came from its traditional distribution business.

Three years ago, Anixter made a big push into building network infrastructure via integration and consulting services and has invested tens of millions of dollars in that area. Another new business area is network education services.
"The next wave of investment is in Asia-Pacific," Wun said.
He said in the past year the company had invested about US$20 million in the emerging markets of Latin America and the Asia-Pacific.

Wun said the Asia-Pacific was already Anixter's fastest growing region where it already had more than 10 percent of the market share. He saw its Asia Pacific business outperforming the company's worldwide growth in the next three years.
Anixter has 18 offices in 10 countries in the region.
Besides warehousing centres for the individual markets, it has three warehousing hubs catering to the region.
In total, Anixter holds US$20 million to US$40 million of stock at any one time in Asia-Pacific, said James Yao, Anixter's vice-president of marketing in the region.
Wun said through its stock management, it aimed to raise the level of service in the industry by delivering products to its customers as quickly as within a day.
Anixter is planning to set up operations in Japan in 1998 and is studying the market needs there, Wun said. Japan would also have its own warehousing centre.

Anixter recently started business in South Korea and expected "active operations in the second quarter this year", he said. It recently set up a warehouse in Seattle in the United States which is already supplying to South Korea and will become a regional hub for Asia-Pacific as well, he said.
